title: no time to explain remastered
text: I just played through this game's main storyline in one session. Here's what I think: The Good: + The beam gun and the flinging shotgun are innovative plattforming mechanics. + The levels are visually varied and generally well designed. Checkpoints are usually placed quite generously and fairly. + Each chapter introduces new temporary environmental mechanics, which makes for a shortwhiled experience. + The overall pacing of the levels is quite good, none of the chapters or mechanics outstay their welcome. + Collecting hats is  a fun way to customise your character and provides a nice layer of additional challenge in most stages. + Some of the hats are downright ridiculous and so is the main stoyline. The humour is definitely debatable, very slapstick-esque and lol-so-random, but I think it's safe to say that if the trailer for this game appeals to you then you will enjoy the plot. + The original soundtrack kicks♥♥♥♥♥and is surprisingly varied. + The voice acting is ridiculously over the top and probably the main contributing factor to this game's hillarity. + The meta-commentary on video games and game design seemed a little out of place, but I enjoyed it regardless. + Steam Workshop support, additional levels, and the challenge of trying to collect all the hats and all the achievements should be enough incentive to keep playing for those masochistic enough to want to do so. The Bad: - In almost every chapter there will be one stage that is extremely hard in comparison to the rest. This seems in part due to these stages having less generous checkpoints than usual or sometimes none at all. These random difficulty spikes can be very frustrating and are a testament to the fact that this was a debut game by a small company. Definitely could have used some more playtesting. - The game keeps its promise to not explain anything. You have to figure out every new mechanic by yourself and make creative use of your movement abilites to forge your path through the levels. This is of course where the challenge of the game comes from, but I think it is safe to say it does not hold your hand. As a result, I sometimes found myself having to cross-references videos of other people's playthroughs to make sure my approach to traversing the level was correct and it was only my execution that sucked. - The bossfights in particular are quite hard. They all have set rotations that you'll have to figure out for yourself. The game generally tries to give visual and auditive clues as to what you should be doing, but oftentimes it is unclear how many stages a fight has. Bosses also never have a healthbar, instead the game relies purely on different visual stages of the bosses' models which makes the progress of the fight feel vague at times. -Playing the game with a controller seemed fine, but there were a few stages where I found myself switching back to mouse and keyboard as the chapter-specific mechanics seemed easier to handle that way. - The main campaign can be finished in around 3-4 hours. This might be a consideration for some people, although as I said the game is overall very enjoyable and shortwhiled. - The original price tag of 15 euros/dollars is a little too high in my opinion. Although it's definitely worth picking up on sale for a reduced price, probably more around the 5-8 euros/dollars mark.

text: The humor was definitely there in the beginning, what with your future self being severely mutilated right in front of you, but after a little while, the humor dies down when you realize that's it. Every level you start off in shows another version of you being dragged off with spurts of blood and screaming in agony, but it starts to get tedious and annoying, especially when you keep dying while trying to figure out how to proceed to the next level. And once that humor is gone, all you're left with is a kind of mediocre platformer. The idea of using your gun's momentum to traverse the area is pretty cool, but it falls kind of flat simply because what sells this game is the weird, quirky randomness of the trailer, not so much the game. I think another major difference here is the controller. It has the full support, but if you're someone like me who always prefers the controller to the mouse and keyboard, you'll have a harder time. Like with almost any FPS game, using the mouse is infinitely more accurate and quicker than trying to orient yourself with the stick. Normally that's not too much of a problem, but when the difference between a success and failure is a split second decision of where to aim the gun, it can be pretty jarring since you have no clear indicator of where you're aiming until you shoot. Not only that, but the stick just feels sluggish anfd I always feel like I'm overcompensating on turns trying to figure out where to orient myself when the mouse would probably feel more fluid. If you fall into my kind of category, where you bought the game because you thought it would be a good laugh, and you prefer the gamepad, the novelty will wear off really quick. This is more like a game that you play with your drinking buddies on the weekends to just laugh at each other's failings. And maybe most importantly, is the price. This game doesn't scream out $15 to me. I feel that's too overpriced. If you really want to get this, I would wait for a sale.

text: I expected this game to be fun, but I've actually been enjoying it even more than I expected.  Games with roguelike elements are known for their high replayability, and Nuclear Throne is no different, but a big part of the replay value in this game is the different abilities of each of the characters.  Transform into an immobile bullet-reflecting cyrstal spire, eat guns and recycle them into ammunition, ensnare enemies in a tangle of thorny vines, cause enemy corpses on screen to explode... each character changes your approach to the game in sometimes subtle and sometimes dramatic ways, and that'sone of the big things that keeps me coming back.  Even though I do have my personal favories... Robot and Melting 4 life!  And death.  Lots and lots of death.

title: one finger death punch
text: A simple yet enjoyable game that I really thought was going to be mediocre,but turns out to be good amounts of fun,Of course,you should't buy this game if you are looking for hours of gameplay,its a crazy over the top experience that I think is cool. There are only 2 controls,your left and right mouse button,and you use them to defeat your enemies.That's it,but there are different modes like "multiround","smash round" to break the monotony.Plus,you can unlock skills to help you in your battles,although sometimes they are disabled in some modes.That's all there is to know about this game. So,do I recommend this?Well,in full price no,because I can't really see much of a reason to play this game for more than 10 hours,you will quickly get bored,so I suggest you pick it up on a 50 or 75% dicount.
